target.title: PR1/5 durable core: residual-gap RFC docs
target.body:
## Context capsule

This is PR1/5 in the durable-core stack. It is docs/RFC only: it proposes a narrow residual-gap durable-core boundary and proof plan for reviewer discussion before any implementation PR claims runtime behavior.

This PR does not publish a release architecture contract. It does not claim shipped runtime behavior, wake replay, CLI/Gateway controls, session handoff, external transport delivery, schema migration, or product retry/resume policy.

## Scope updated 2026-07-15

- Reframes the architecture page as **Durable Core Residual-Gap Architecture Proposal**.
- Reframes the proof page as **Durable Core Residual-Gap Test Plan**.
- Renames the new public docs routes from retired prerelease slugs to proposal slugs:
  - `/specs/durable-core-proposal-architecture`
  - `/specs/durable-core-proposal-test-plan`
- Aligns `docs/docs.json`, `docs/docs_map.md`, and the zh-CN glossary with those final titles/routes.
- Explicitly positions the RFC as complementary to existing TaskFlow/database-first ownership, not a competing shipped persistence contract.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can accept long-running work, delegate it to subagents, defer it through waits, route it through channels, and recover after restarts. Existing owners already persist important state. The remaining proposal is about residual cross-owner invariants: stable work refs, auditable events, owner/lease expiry, terminal immutability, wake/attention routing, delivery evidence boundaries, inspection, and fail-closed recovery.

## Non-scope

- No runtime behavior.
- No database/schema migration.
- No CLI/Gateway controls.
- No worker loop or wake replay implementation.
- No plugin/channel delivery behavior.
- No Task Flow or Workboard product feature implementation.
- No claim that external transport delivery is covered by internal session handoff.

## Current head and proof

- Current PR head: `c54be40f5c3ddb87b5c1ac6bf4622d317a848fbd`
- Base branch: `release/2026.7.1`
- Diff surface: docs/navigation/glossary only.

| Gate | Command | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Docs map | `pnpm docs:map:check` | passed |
| Targeted MDX/docs JSON | `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs/specs/durable-core-proposal-architecture.md docs/specs/durable-core-proposal-test-plan.md docs/docs.json` | passed |
| Docs links | `pnpm docs:check-links` | passed; `broken_links=0` |
| Diff hygiene | `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` | passed |
| Stale wording scan | `rg -n "beta3|Beta 3|2026\\.7\\.1|Release Architecture|Release Test Plan|release stack|official release|shipped release|User Promise" <touched durable docs/config>` | passed; no matches in the touched durable proposal files/routes/glossary |

`pnpm docs:check-i18n-glossary` was also run. It failed on unrelated branch-base glossary omissions across existing docs (for example `Raft`, `Attach CLI`, `Gateway protocol`, provider/plugin labels), not on the durable-core proposal titles added here.

## ClawSweeper concerns addressed

- Release-specific contract: removed/reframed as an RFC proposal and residual-gap boundary.
- Stale prerelease route wording: removed from the new public docs routes.
- Page/glossary mismatch: glossary source strings now match the final durable-core page titles.
- Ownership overlap: the docs now explicitly build on TaskFlow/database-first owners and describe only residual cross-owner contracts.

## Remaining review risk

A durable-work owner or maintainer still needs to decide whether this residual-gap boundary is the right upstream architecture direction. This PR only makes the proposal reviewable; it does not implement or assert the behavior.
